key_insight: A unified analytical model can diagnose where photoelectrochemical cell losses occur and turn that diagnosis into rational design rules for both BIJ and SEJ devices.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers compare materials and architectures on a common basis, quantify bottlenecks from experimental J–V curves, and target upgrades such as co-catalysts, nanostructuring, or better band alignment.
method: Unified loss-analysis model for BIJ and SEJ photoelectrodes
Efficiency maps and ideal/real J–V curves to locate performance limits
Fit experimental data to decompose losses into thermodynamic, optical, recombination, and interfacial terms
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation against state-of-the-art literature across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries.
watch_item: The model is only as reliable as the fit quality and underlying assumptions, so complex real-device physics or poorly characterized interfaces may limit quantitative loss attribution.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
